questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Stop your wheels from locking up.
Prevent your vehicle from speeding up on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: When should you do an after-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: You must inspect your vehicle after every trip. Complete a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: How should you do a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: You don't need to check all items every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way each time. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you don't forget to check anything.

questions.question: A 10-foot load needs at least how many tie-downs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. But all cargo needs at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: What does an Individual Vehicle Distance Record NOT need to include?

options.text: The number of vehicles you passed

questions.correctAnswerText: The number of vehicles you passed
questions.explanation: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record must include trip dates and total distance traveled. It does not need to include the number of vehicles you passed.

questions.question: What is required to haul hanging meat in a refrigerated truck?

options.text: It is good experience for new drivers.
You need to be a skilled driver.
It is illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to be a skilled driver.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable cargo because it has a high center of gravity and swings, which affects how you handle the vehicle. Only skilled drivers should transport it.

questions.question: Is it safe to reach for a phone while driving?

options.text: Yes, if you are alone in the vehicle.
Yes, if you plan to use hands-free.
No, even if you plan to use hands-free.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, even if you plan to use hands-free.
questions.explanation: Do not reach for your phone while driving. Your phone must be close and easy to reach without moving from your seat. Unsafe reaching is dangerous, even if you plan to use hands-free.

questions.question: Should dual tires touch each other?
questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: Are wheels with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if a professional did the repairs.
Yes, if the repair looks solid.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they are not safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use wheels or rims with welding repairs. Replace them before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do shortly after changing a tire?

options.text: Stop to check the lug nuts are tight.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to check the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you change a tire, stop a short time later and check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Keep cargo in a large box.
Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
Stop cargo from falling out of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed on all sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle moves.

questions.question: Which of these surfaces is most slippery?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when the weather is warm enough to melt ice slightly. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: When driving a truck that requires a CDL:

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must wear a safety belt at all times when driving a commercial truck.

questions.question: If you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test, you will:

options.text: Lose extra points on your final score.
Automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will cause you to automatically fail the test.

questions.question: When alley docking, what should you do first?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop your vehicle parallel to the outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking area.

questions.question: When going down a long hill, you should brake by:

options.text: Using mostly brakes and sometimes downshifting.
Downshifting first, then using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting first, then using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before using the brakes on a downhill slope. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail. Engine braking in a lower gear is the main way to control your speed going downhill.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks:

options.text: Usually have a low center of gravity.
Usually have a high center of gravity.
Are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually have a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks usually have high centers of gravity, which requires special care while driving. The cargo can also shift during transport.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Jump quickly from low to high.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slowly.
questions.explanation: After starting your engine, watch the gauges. The coolant temperature should rise slowly to the normal operating range.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: May need to swerve out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swerve out of the way.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you do not have enough space to stop, swerving may be your safest option.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air:

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if the pressure gets too high. If this happens, there is a problem in the system that a mechanic should check.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early. Signal well before you turn or change lanes.
Signal continuously. Keep your signal on until the turn is complete.
Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, you don't need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, you don't need to signal.
questions.explanation: When using turn signals, signal well before turning or changing lanes. Keep the signal on throughout the turn or lane change. Turn it off after you complete your move. Always signal, even if no one is nearby.

questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill, your best option to stop is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use an escape ramp.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill grade, look for an escape ramp. This is the safest way to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: Compared to talking on a cell phone while driving, texting while driving is:
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on the phone. Texting takes your attention away from the road and your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safe vehicle operation?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Check your vehicle before driving to make sure it is in good working condition.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Air tanks are shared between both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. Both systems share one set of brake controls, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Inspect your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts may indicate they are loose.

questions.question: Do NOT base your decision to shift gears on:

options.text: What the vehicle next to you is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What the vehicle next to you is doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your speed. Shift up when your engine reaches the top of its rpm range or when you reach the right speed for the next gear. Never shift based on what other vehicles are doing.

questions.question: A driver with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: A person who likes fresh air.

questions.correctAnswerText: A distracted driver.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs that a driver may be impaired by alcohol, drugs, drowsiness, or illness. One sign is that they have their windows down in cold weather. This is a clue they may be trying to stay awake.

questions.question: One way to prevent hydroplaning on wet roads is to:

options.text: Keep good tread depth on your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep good tread depth on your tires.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is more likely if your tire pressure is too low or your tire tread is worn. Good tire tread helps water drain away. If you start to hydroplane, release the accelerator and push in the clutch.

questions.question: Bridges usually freeze:

options.text: Only when temperatures drop well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular roadways. Be extra careful on bridges when temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect cargo from animals
questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect cargo from weather.

questions.question: What should you do if the brakes cannot build up hydraulic pressure?

options.text: Hold the brake pedal down as far as it will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift.
questions.explanation: If your brakes cannot build pressure, try downshifting, pumping the brakes, and using the emergency brake.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice on road surfaces is called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. The road may look wet, not icy. Be very careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving skills test:

options.text: You do not need to use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed for
You must use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed for
It does not matter which vehicle you use

questions.correctAnswerText: You must use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed for
questions.explanation: You must take the on-road test with the type of vehicle you want to be licensed for.

questions.question: How can you prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting to move?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal
Place the vehicle in second gear
Use the parking brake when stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal to prevent rolling backward.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to change lanes:

options.text: Do not worry about other drivers
Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe
Change lanes quickly, even if it means cutting off another driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe
questions.explanation: Check traffic, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, a driver should:

options.text: Only set the parking brake if on a slope

questions.correctAnswerText: Always set the parking brake
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Friction between tires and the road
The time it takes to activate the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Friction between tires and the road
questions.explanation: Traction is friction between your tires and the road. You need good traction for braking and steering.

questions.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, the belt should be checked to ensure it is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Properly tightened
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor drive belt before each drive. Check that it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.correctAnswerText: May not affect
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other.

questions.question: Bracing is used to:

options.text: Make items stand taller in a trailer.
Stop items from moving in a trailer.
Make it easier to unload items from a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop items from moving in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing stop cargo from shifting during transport. Blocking is placed in front, behind, and on the sides of cargo. Bracing connects the top of cargo to the floor and sides of the trailer to prevent movement.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of tie-down equipment?
questions.correctAnswerText: Velcro
questions.explanation: You must use the correct number of tie-downs to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer. Tie-down equipment includes ropes, straps, and chains.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should ensure that the ____ turn on automatically when air pressure falls below 45 psi.
questions.correctAnswerText: Spring brakes
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that spring brakes engage automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Test this by chocking the wheels and releasing air by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve pops out and spring brakes engage.

questions.question: When approaching a vehicle for a pre-trip inspection, a driver should look under the vehicle to:

options.text: See if the vehicle is on an incline.
Check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
See if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting your vehicle, check its general condition and look for damage or leaning. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Check around the vehicle for hazards like people, other vehicles, or low wires or tree limbs.

questions.question: If you doubt you have enough space to safely drive under a bridge or sign, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive more slowly.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure your vehicle will fit under overhead objects, slow down and take a different route if possible.

questions.question: If a truck is equipped with one, a trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: If a tractor-trailer has a trailer brake hand valve, you can use it to stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a concern since it is stopped.
Is only a concern if passengers are getting off the bus.
Is a concern even if you cannot see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a concern even if you cannot see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful when driving near a stopped bus. Passengers may be nearby, and the bus may block your view or theirs.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Tell the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
Estimate how heavy the load is on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are inspecting and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer:

options.text: The trailer doors should be opened.
The trailer doors should not be opened.
A large, heavy blanket should be put over the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer doors should not be opened.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire, especially if the cargo includes hazardous materials. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen and can make it grow larger.

questions.question: Front tires must have a tread depth of at least ____ in every major groove.
questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles need a tread depth of 4/32 of an inch in every major groove on front tires. Other tires need a tread depth of 2/32 of an inch.
